summary: Under Disposición 002-2026, in force since 16 February 2026, Nicaragua sorts nationalities into two categories. Category A — 69 nationalities including the US, Canada, the UK, most of the EU, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Saudi Arabia and Qatar — needs no visa and buys a USD 10 tourist card on arrival for up to 90 days. Category C — 128 nationalities including Mexico, Colombia, New Zealand, China, India and Cuba — needs a "consulted" visa approved in advance by immigration in Managua. Citizens of El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras move freely under the CA-4 agreement.

declarations.text: Every traveller, or the head of a travelling family, entering or leaving Nicaragua must complete a customs Traveller's Declaration. Nicaragua's customs service (DGA) lets you fill it in online and print it, from three days before you travel; it asks, among other things, whether you carry cash or valuables worth USD 10,000 or more.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says electronic smoking devices such as e-cigarettes are banned: you cannot import, export, sell, store or use them, with or without nicotine, and customs can confiscate them at the border.
The UK Foreign Office says there is a prohibition on the possession and use of drones, and that Law 1230 of December 2024 requires people who have drones to hand them in to the authorities.
The UK Foreign Office says possession of even small quantities of drugs can lead to imprisonment.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says credit cards are usually accepted but ATMs may not be available outside major cities, and that US dollars are easily exchanged at banks or official exchange offices. The UK Foreign Office says the US dollar is the only foreign currency freely exchangeable and warns against changing money on the street.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal for foreigners to take part in any political activity, and joining a protest, attending political meetings or campaigns, or using the national blue-and-white colours in a campaign can lead to arrest, detention or deportation. It says foreign nationals have been affected by violent crime, including attacks on people in vehicles and 'express kidnapping' in unauthorised taxis, and advises using radio-dispatched or red-plate authorised taxis and not visiting markets and bus stations on foot after dark.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must pay an arrival tax of 10 US dollars in cash, and that the US dollar is the only foreign currency freely exchangeable in Nicaragua.

The UK Foreign Office says the 90-day visa-free period for Nicaragua, El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras starts when you enter any of them and does not restart when you cross between them, and that if you overstay you may get a fine.

Canada's travel advice cites UN reports that the authorities prevent certain people from entering or leaving Nicaragua for political reasons and arbitrarily search personal phones and computers for anti-government content. Both Canada and the UK Foreign Office say political activity by foreigners is illegal and can lead to detention or deportation.

The UK Foreign Office says several volcanoes are active, in particular San Cristóbal, Masaya, Cerro Negro, Telica and Concepción on Ometepe Island, and advises not to hike on volcanoes without an experienced guide. It says the hurricane season normally runs from June to November.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Nicaragua?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Under Disposición 002-2026, in force since 16 February 2026, Nicaragua has two categories. Category A — 69 nationalities including the US, Canada, the UK, most of the EU, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Saudi Arabia and Qatar — needs no visa and simply buys a USD 10 tourist card on arrival, valid for up to 90 days. Category C — 128 nationalities including Mexico, Colombia, New Zealand, China, India and Cuba — needs a "consulted" visa approved in advance by immigration in Managua. Salvadoran, Guatemalan and Honduran citizens move freely under CA-4.

faq.question: What is the Nicaraguan tourist card and how much does it cost?
faq.answer: It is a USD 10 entry card, not a visa; Category A visitors can stay up to 90 days. The UK Foreign Office says the 10 US dollar arrival tax must be paid in cash.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Nicaragua?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt visitors are normally granted up to 90 days, and that allowance is shared with El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras under the CA-4 agreement. Before it runs out you can ask the Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería — in Managua or at any departmental office — for up to 90 more days, for a USD 25 fee.

faq.question: How does the CA-4 agreement affect my trip?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says the 90-day visa-free period for El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua starts when you enter any of the four and does not restart when you cross borders between them; you still go through immigration checks at each border.

faq.question: What is a "consulted" visa (visa consultada)?
faq.answer: It is the visa for Category C nationalities — 128 of them under Disposición 002-2026, including Mexico, Colombia, China, India and Cuba (ordinary passports). The consulate cannot decide on its own: the application goes to immigration headquarters in Managua for prior authorization. Since February 2026 you can apply and pay online at tramitesconsulares.mint.gob.ni and download the approved visa, with no consulate visit, or apply by email to solicitudes@mint.gob.ni. Immigration asks for a passport valid for at least six months, a letter requesting the visa, a police certificate and a notarized undertaking to cover your costs.

faq.question: Is Nicaragua safe to visit right now?
faq.answer: Canada says to exercise a high degree of caution because of the political situation, the potential for civil unrest and crime. The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal for foreigners to take part in any political activity, including protests, and that you can be arrested, detained or deported for it.
